title: Unify typography, iconography and shape tokens for surface cohesion
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background:
The current token surface has grown organically: separate typography scales, icon pixel sizes, spacing units (px-based), and multiple radius/elevation aliases. This has led to visual drift between controls, inconsistent hit targets, and brittle responsive behavior. Several components (tables, buttons, chips) render slightly out-of-step across breakpoints because icon size and line-height are not coordinated with spacing and corner radii.

Problem statement:
We need a single, coherent token strategy that ties type scale, iconography sizing, spacing, and shape (radius) to a proportional system so components retain cohesion across density modes and responsive breakpoints. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc per-component overrides, simplify token consumption for engineers, and improve accessibility (consistent touch targets and visual rhythm).

Goals:
- Introduce an em/rem-aware typography scale that maps to container sizing tokens.
- Standardize iconography sizes to align with type steps and spacing increments.
- Move spacing/radius tokens from absolute px-only values to proportional aliases (eg. space-1 = 0.25rem, radius-sm = 0.25 * control-height).
- Re-bake elevation/shadow deltas to maintain perceived depth at different densities (compact, default, roomy).
- Provide migration aliases for current tokens to minimize breaking changes for components.

Proposal summary:
1) Type: adopt a 1.125 modular scale with named steps (type-xs, type-sm, type-base, type-md, type-lg, type-xl). Tokens expressed in rem with explicit line-height tokens (line-xs, line-sm, line-base, etc.).
2) Icons: derive icon sizes from the type steps. For example icon-sm = type-sm cap-height approx, icon-md = type-base cap-height, icon-lg = type-lg cap-height. Provide pixel fallbacks for legacy rendering in Canvas/Bitmap contexts.
3) Spacing/Radius: define spacing units as space-0..space-8 in rem. Radius tokens reference spacing values via descriptive aliases (radius-tight = space-1, radius-default = space-2, radius-soft = space-3) and provide control-based radii (control-radius = 0.125 * control-height).
4) Elevation: create elevation token family (e0..e5) with two delta sets (compact, default). Recalculate shadow blur/offset/opacities so that e1 in compact matches perceived depth of e2 in default.
5) Token aliases & migration: keep legacy token names mapped to new tokens for at least two releases. Provide a compatibility stylesheet and migration guide.

Trade-offs and considerations:
- Pros: single source of truth, fewer bespoke overrides, easier responsive behavior, better accessibility consistency.
- Cons: some components will require small visual adjustments; teams will need to update snapshots and possibly adjust layout calculations that assumed px-only tokens. There is a risk of visual regressions in third-party embeds that read raw pixel values.

Success metrics:
- Reduce number of per-component token overrides by 60% in the component library within 2 cycles.
- No accessibility regressions: maintain WCAG AA contrast and minimum 44px touch targets for primary controls.
- Developer adoption: 80% of new components use proportional tokens within one cycle after rollout.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): token specification document, Figma variables proof-of-concept, and migration alias mapping.
- Phase 2 (2–4 weeks): implement tokens in core primitives (button, input, chip, avatar, icon component) and update docs.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): component library migration (tables, cards, menus) plus QA and visual regression checks.
- Phase 4 (1 week): release compatibility stylesheet and communicate deprecation plan.

Dependencies:
- ENG-18921 (runtime design tokens ingestion pipeline) for token distribution automation.
- PM-402 (design system release coordination) for scheduling and communications.

Artifacts and links:
- Figma working file: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood-DS/typography-icon-shape-tokens
- Spec doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/Type+Icon+Shape+Token+Proposal
- Migration checklist (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/Redwood-DS-Migration
- Visual regression dashboard (Percy): https://percy.io/redwood/ds-token-migration

Accessibility note:
Whenever spacing or type adjustments change a component's hit target or label wrapping, we will run a focused accessibility pass (keyboard focus order, screen reader label checks, and contrast verification).
